BusinessModel: Company makes paracetamol API, the pain-and-fever powder inside tablets. Sells the powder to drug makers in India and abroad. Runs one plant in Gujarat.
RevenueStreams: Paracetamol API, near 100% of revenue (FY25); minor finished dosage/other (data not found)
Expenses: Raw materials (para-aminophenol, phenol) dominant, ~60-70% (data not found precisely); low employee base; nearly debt-free so minimal finance cost
TAM: Global paracetamol API market low single-digit USD billion (industry estimate)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Paracetamol API price cycle; raw material costs linked to crude; plant utilisation and receivable collection (197 debtor days FY25)

BusinessModel: Company makes medicines for other pharma brands as India's largest contract drug manufacturer by volume. Produces tablets, capsules, injections and gummies at large plants. Charges brands for manufacturing.
RevenueStreams: Contract manufacturing of formulations, bulk of revenue (FY25); trade generics/other minor (~Rs 4120-4170 cr consolidated revenue FY25)
Expenses: Raw materials (APIs, excipients) major head; employee costs significant; working-capital heavy (101 inventory days, 59 debtor days FY25)
TAM: Indian pharma contract manufacturing market ~USD 15-20 billion, high single/low double digit CAGR (industry estimate)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Contract volumes and pricing with top customers (top ~10% of customers = ~47% of revenue FY25); plant utilisation; API/raw material costs

BusinessModel: Bank lends small amounts to rural and low-income customers. Microfinance loans formed the historic core and gold loans now grow fast. Funds itself with deposits.
RevenueStreams: Microfinance lending (historic core, FY25); gold loans (fast growing, +106% YoY); other retail/corporate loans and deposits; fee income minor
Expenses: Provisions and credit costs (the FY25 loss driver); interest paid on deposits; branch and employee overheads
TAM: Indian MFI portfolio ~Rs 4-5 lakh crore and gold loan market ~Rs 6+ lakh crore (FY25 industry estimates)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Credit costs on microfinance book; NIM on gold+microfinance mix; deposit cost and overhead ratio

BusinessModel: Company makes high-voltage electrical gear - busbars, transformers, switchgear - that connects power plants, data centres and grids. Sells mostly to clients across ~80 countries. Listed February 2025.
RevenueStreams: Busducts/busbar systems, transformers, switchgear and grid-connection equipment; FY25 consolidated revenue ~Rs 311-337 cr with ~Rs 100 cr PAT; FY26 crossed ~Rs 1007 cr consolidated
Expenses: Raw materials (copper, aluminium, steel) dominant; employee and engineering costs; almost debt-free (FY25)
TAM: Global busbar/energy-transition equipment market multi-billion USD annually (DRHP-based estimate)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Data-centre and grid capex orders in export markets; busbar mix and margin expansion (OPM 18% to 26% FY24-FY25 standalone); new capacity execution from IPO funds

BusinessModel: Company builds wire harnesses and electrical parts for military and commercial aircraft. Sells engineering-and-manufacturing services to Boeing, Lockheed Martin and Bell. Listed after demerger in 2024.
RevenueStreams: Aerospace & defence engineering (wire harnesses, sheet metal, assembly) dominant (FY25 ~Rs 259 cr standalone); space systems new (~Rs 400 cr contract FY26); semiconductor entry nascent
Expenses: Raw materials (wires, connectors, metals) major; employee costs significant; moderate finance costs
TAM: Indian aerospace & defence manufacturing projected to grow several-fold over the decade (Make-in-India estimates)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Wire-harness volumes for global OEMs; new space vertical; operating leverage on Bengaluru facility

BusinessModel: Company ships dry bulk cargo such as coal, grain and fertilizers by sea for clients at India and Sri Lanka ports. Focuses on non-major ports on India's west coast. Listed August 2025.
RevenueStreams: Dry bulk shipping freight, bulk of revenue (FY25 standalone Rs 584 cr); port-side logistics services minor
Expenses: Vessel operating costs (bunker fuel, crew, maintenance) dominant; charter hire; port and jetty costs
TAM: Indian dry bulk coastal/short-sea shipping at west-coast ports, multi-million tonne annual trade (DRHP-based)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Freight/charter rates (biggest swing); vessel utilisation and fleet size; fuel and port costs

BusinessModel: Company blends, fills and processes refrigerant and industrial gases for air-conditioners and factories. Buys gas in bulk, blends it, and sells in cylinders. Also serves fire-protection, pharma and electronics buyers. Listed January 2025.
RevenueStreams: Refrigerant gases (core, FY25 total Rs 377 cr); specialty gases for fire protection, medical, electronics growing; FY26 ~Rs 434 cr total
Expenses: Purchase of imported bulk gases dominant; blending/filling power and logistics costs; low employee intensity
TAM: Indian fluorochemicals/specialty gases market USD 675-725 million by 2029, 16-18% CAGR from 2024 (Value Research)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Refrigerant volumes on HVAC/AC demand; purchase-vs-sale gas spread; new high-margin specialty gas lines

BusinessModel: Company makes precision tooling and components that aircraft makers and repair shops need to build and service planes. Sells to Airbus, Boeing, GE, Rolls-Royce and Dassault across 2500+ SKUs. Listed December 2024.
RevenueStreams: Aero tooling and precision components for OEM/MRO, dominant (FY25 consolidated ~Rs 241-260 cr, PAT ~Rs 77 cr); GSE and mechanical assemblies; defence/power/semiconductor nascent
Expenses: Raw materials (speciality metals) major; skilled employee costs high; almost debt-free
TAM: Global aerospace tooling/MRO precision parts multi-billion USD annually; India MRO ~USD 4-6 billion by 2030 (industry estimates)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Aero tooling/components for global OEMs and MRO; new defence/semiconductor verticals; operating leverage from Bengaluru expansion

BusinessModel: Company makes transmission parts for vehicles - torque converters, transfer cases for 4WD SUVs and EV transmission units. Also assembles turbochargers with BorgWarner. Sells to Tata Motors and Mahindra. Listed March 2023.
RevenueStreams: Torque converters and transfer cases (core, FY25 Rs 219 cr standalone); turbochargers/EGR with BorgWarner growing; EV transmissions nascent
Expenses: Raw materials (aluminium, steel) major; employee costs moderate; nearly debt-free
TAM: Indian auto components industry ~USD 70-80 billion FY24 (ACMA estimate)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Transfer-case/torque-converter volumes for Tata/Mahindra SUVs; BorgWarner turbocharger ramp; EV transmission orders

BusinessModel: Company makes test-and-measuring instruments - analog panel meters, multimeters, transmitters - plus industrial control products and aluminium die-cast parts. Sells ~two-thirds overseas through plants in India and Poland. Listed August 2023.
RevenueStreams: Test & measuring instruments and industrial control products, core (FY23 consolidated ~Rs 570 cr); aluminium HPDC (Lumel) significant; ~66% exports
Expenses: Raw materials (metals, electronics) major; employee costs at India+Poland plants; almost debt-free
TAM: Global test & measurement instruments market ~USD 25-30 billion (mid-2020s industry estimate)
PL_Top3_Contributors: Test/measurement and control product sales (export-led); HPDC segment demand in Europe; INR-EUR/USD currency moves on ~66% overseas revenue
